text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B quotes the article directly: \"If the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault—the driver or the manufacturer?\" and engages with it", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay integrates a direct quotation from the source article to support its argument, whereas Essay A only paraphrases the article without citing specific text."}, {"evidence": "Essay B develops multiple distinct reasons (technology failure, driver distraction, liability) each in its own paragraph with elaboration", "quality": "Organized argument structure", "description": "The essay presents a clear introduction, body paragraphs each devoted to a separate supporting point, and a conclusion, giving it a coherent structure that Essay A lacks."}, {"evidence": "Essay B explores scenarios like technology freezing, the driver falling asleep, and who is at fault in an accident", "quality": "Reasoned development of claims", "description": "The essay explains the reasoning behind each objection with concrete hypothetical situations, while Essay A mostly asserts opinions without developing them."}, {"evidence": "Essay B maintains a consistent argumentative tone focused on safety and reliability throughout", "quality": "Focused argumentation", "description": "The essay stays on its central thesis about the dangers and unreliability of driverless cars, whereas Essay A wanders into tangential complaints about cost, laziness, and affordability."}, {"evidence": "Essay B uses rhetorical questions and a closing appeal that ties back to the safety theme", "quality": "Effective conclusion", "description": "The essay ends with a pointed rhetorical question that reinforces its main argument, while Essay A trails off without a clear concluding statement."}]}
